title: Memory Decoder at Scale — paper view
subtitle: The mechanism as Wei et al. describe it: retrieval happens once, offline, to build a training signal; inference is two frozen forward passes plus a fixed-weight interpolation. Lane = canonical stage (METHODOLOGY-SKELETON §2.2); empty lanes are stages this mechanism does not have.
source: Wei et al. 2026, Memory Decoder at Scale (arXiv:2607.27919v1)   ·   every anchor re-located in the paper txt during verification (59 paper-side assertions, 50 ✓ / 3 ✗ / 5 ◐ / 1 ?)
legend_notes: B1-B5 are empty on purpose, and A4 is the busiest lane in this whole project. The dense retrieval (self-query top-K over the datastore) happens once, offline, while building the datastore and its distribution supervision -- not at query time. This is the case the whole A/B (formation/mobilization) split was named after: calling it a 'retrieval stage' would be wrong, since at inference the Faiss index and datastore are never loaded (txt:259).

β is NOT an undocumented hyperparameter: Appendix Table 9 and Table 10 both list 'Memory loss weight' = 0.5 for every backbone size and for domain memory -- an earlier reading that only checked the main text missed this.

α is also not a blind default: Appendix F sweeps a 0:0.05:1 grid (21 points, Fig.11) and Table 15 records the per-task selected value; the paper's own text (§4 end) says it is 'fixed for testing' after this validation-set search.

Domain memory (biology/law/finance) reuses the exact same A4-A6 pipeline as general memory; the only extra step is one continued-pretraining pass over the domain corpus so the backbone that extracts keys is domain-adapted (§3.3).
